author: Warren
text:
Dr Swing,

The last part of the Journey always seems the hardest. We are battle worn, tired and feel vulnerable.

That overwhelming urge to come "full circle" with any of our endeavours is what keeps us going. I know your frustration, It is like a splinter in your mind. The hardest thing is to accept is we may not be there yet, where others think we are. Being put on a pedestal is like being judged on every post you make. The most important thing you want to give to any reader is the correct information, this really exposes you in the raw. You are right or wrong, simple as that.

It is one thing for the market to prove you wrong, but it is another to make it public too.

As traders we must accept that until we master ourselves, we can not master the market.

you can be technically right 100% at chart reading. But what about your state of mind at that time, are there any life distractions, do you feel under pressure to perform. Have you had an argument with a loved one, is your boss winding you up.

The further up life's ladder you go, the more pressure to perform is on your shoulders.

All the professionals I have ever known, still spend countless hours going over the basics. EVEN those at the top of there game.

I have found the best way to deal with my demons is to face them FULL on. With more persistence and energy than before. so, yes post in your journal, empty your thoughts in here. For our most vulnerable moments can be the most enlightening.

Regards

Warren

Ok, this post is an insight into one method of how I try to find my trade opps.

I read the charts to find zone engulfs rather than just DBR/RBD engulfs as this gives the desired R:R.

I see the charts in terms of Poles and Flags and I'm looking to the SR transition level between the PAZs. This trade level has to be an M1 SD zone 3-4 pips wide and providing an FO to the above/below FTR/FL. I then trade the return to this level, giving me a potentially massive R:R. author: strudl
text:
DrSwing wrote: Well guys and gals it's time for me to fess up!

I'll be a year here on RTM next week, and for months now I can smell and even touch the other side, but I just cant break through. Right now I find I am spinning my wheels, basically going around in circles, in frustration. So very often I have felt so close to being at one with the markets, only to awake the following day a stranger again. I am not learning anything new and not having any new aha moments, and this week in particular I just seem to have a mental block. Sure I can read the past PA all day and all night, but I just can't trade the hard right edge! Not even on Forextester!

When I first joined I posted quite a lot, but then I found that the more I learned the more difficult it became to post. You see, I wanted to be able to help lead the way, but I found that my posting was often inaccurate and therefore misleading to members. So I would only post the things that I was definite about. This made it very difficult for me to make comments on posts or attempt to answer members questions. So I worked harder in silence, digging into the charts in order to be able to make posts that would add value to the forum.

Now heading into my second year, I feel something needs to change. My plan is to start posting regularly again with you all clearly knowing that I am just a mickey mouse trader who is still learning. Even if my posts don't help anyone maybe it will at least help shift my own mental block. Maybe I need the forum now more than it needs me. So please be aware that I am further from being a master trader than most of you posting here, and that everything I post is just my own probably misguided understanding.

Thank you If for your continued support and your patience with our silence.

God Bless all drswing

Thank you Dr. Swing for this post! It was just the push i needed. I am shure you gonna arrive to the other side in no time! Lets crack this market thingy! ~^o^~

text:
rexed9999 wrote: Hi Dr,

Please can you clarify on how you drew those boxes on the first chart? I understand these are PAZ but how exactly do you go about defining and drawing them?

Please can you also clarify on how / what you look for to draw that S/R line?

Thanks, Rex

Hi Rex, sure, I will get to that in a following post, but first this:) Something struck me in a post from Hotrod this morning about himself.

HotRod wrote:.................. I need to loosen up my thought process on price and FTRs. I am still wanting price to have defined rigid rules and then obey those rules.......................

My understanding is that price is not a monthly, weekly, or daily event that happens the same on each occasion. Price is a story that unfolds through time, and each event plays out differently on each occasion as price adapts to it's surroundings. This is why they say that understanding the markets is more of an art than a science. So once you understand all the elements of price reading (the science) that are thought here in RTM, you then use that science to decipher (the art) the unfolding story. The story is always about the ITs moving price from source to destination while playing tricks to hide the route they are taking from the reader. This is why the often double back and set traps to cover their tracks and confuse the tracker. They will not use the identical paths and identical tricks on each occasion.

What I am trying to put accross here, is that price events can be similar, but seldom the same. This is why Hotrod's statement is so important to grasp.

text: Though we have all come to trading to make "handy" money, my advice to beginners is to look for the understanding first, then the money will follow. Trade your understanding and it will give you natural entries and exits. If you have to look too hard to find a trade instead of the trade finding you, then you have to keep working on your understanding.
